engagement_title: NIGHTFORM, Low Beam single drop: pull six beats from one night drive take and hold them to one grade, cut the release video and its vertical, recover the wordmark, and reprint the sleeve card across six formats
vertical: Music, film, publishing and media. Self released electronic single from an independent artist in Portland, Oregon, going to streaming, to the vertical short video feeds, and on vinyl and cassette through independent record shops.
real_brief_anchor: Anchor: the Freelancer.com post quoted in the ledger grounding_note, from a short form vertical video creator looking for a freelance editor to turn raw night footage into a post ready package with, in the poster's own words, on brand colour, a scroll stopping cover, and captions for the vertical short video feeds. The real post named a person, a handle and the editing app; all three are laundered to the coined fictional artist NIGHTFORM, with platform names replaced by the generic vertical short video feeds. The real post is thin because the poster described only the last mile. The fuller commission that client genuinely needed is the one written here: the still imagery for the release comes out of the same take as the video, so the frames and the cut have to be one piece of art direction rather than two jobs; the sleeve card that ships with the physical editions exists only as the printer's PDF from the previous release and has to be reprinted across six formats; and the wordmark survives only as a flat image. CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) is what makes that fuller job honest: a press PDF can be reverse engineered into a live merge template headlessly, HTML authoring returns a native editable Express document at mixed canvas sizes, and an ink level trace recovers a real mark rather than inventing one.
client_one_liner: I have one forty five second take shot out a car window at eleven at night, and it has to become the whole look of this record: the stills, the video, the vertical, the sleeve card and the captions.
client_brief:
NIGHTFORM, Low Beam single drop

I make electronic music and I put my own records out. The next single is called Low Beam and it drops in five weeks. I have one piece of footage and it is the entire visual identity of this release.

The footage is one take, about forty five seconds, shot out of the passenger window on a two lane road north of Portland at around eleven at night. Wet asphalt, sodium lamps, a stretch of tunnel near the end. It is the mood of the record exactly. I need six strong stills out of it to carry the release, and they have to look like six frames of one night rather than six frames I happened to like. At the moment they do not, because the light changes down the road.

I need a short cut of the take for the feeds, and a tall version of that cut for the vertical feed, because that is where the record actually gets found. The tall one has to still be about the road. Nothing stretched and nothing enlarged.

My last release had a printed card that goes in the sleeve and out to the shops. My printer holds that artwork as a PDF and nothing else. I need that card again for this release, six of them, one per format: the vinyl, the cassette, the two digital editions, the shop copy and the press copy. Each carries its own title line, catalogue number, format and date.

My wordmark exists only as a flat picture on a black square. I need it back as artwork I can put on anything at any size, including over the frames.

And I need the caption lines from my script as an overlay set I can edit myself, because the words keep moving right up to the drop.

Deep and cinematic, not clean and commercial. But I still want to be able to see the road.
price_band_and_audience: Self released independent electronic single, no label, streaming first listeners aged roughly 19 to 34, physical editions at 12 to 28 dollars through independent record shops. The band is load bearing: at this level the release is bought on mood and on the sense that one person made it, so the look has to be dark, grainy, cinematic and slightly rough. The identical assets graded bright, clean, saturated and evenly lit would read as a car commercial or a stock library reel, and on an electronic release that misfile is fatal in a way no technical gate catches. Push the other way into total blackness and unreadable type and the record disappears in a feed that is watched at arm's length on a phone in daylight. A posted job of this shape runs 900 to 1,800 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.about: NIGHTFORM is a self released electronic project built on mood: late, atmospheric, cinematic tracks that sound like driving at night. The next single, Low Beam, is bought on feeling and on the sense that one person made the whole thing, so every visual has to carry the same nocturnal weight as the music.

The look has to be dark, grainy and slightly rough, never bright, clean and commercial, which would read as a car advert or a stock reel. Total blackness is the other failure: the road still has to be legible on a phone in daylight.
brand_identity.typography: A clean geometric or grotesque sans set tight and quiet, letting the imagery carry the mood. Captions and the artist name stay legible over dark moving frames at arm's length. No script, no ornament, no filmic distress on the letterforms.
brand_identity.voice: Spare and evocative, closer to a liner note than a sales line. Example line the brand would write: "Low Beam. Recorded from the passenger seat, north of the city, around eleven at night."

It has to be recovered as usable artwork. The previous release's sleeve card exists only as the printer's press PDF, and the whole visual identity for this single comes out of one forty five second night take.
brand_identity.values: One person, one mood, made without a label. The artist changes the words up to the drop date and cannot re commission, so anything text bearing has to stay editable.

assets_supplied.name: nightform_low_beam_take.mov (one take, about 45s, 3840x2160, 24fps)
assets_supplied.kind: A single continuous handheld capture out of a moving car's passenger window at night, sodium lit two lane road, wet asphalt, ending in a lit tunnel.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The whole record, one take out the passenger window. Everything comes from this."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The road sits well left of centre for most of the take, and the last third runs into the lit tunnel where the exposure ramps hard, making that passage simultaneously the brightest and the most motion dense in the file while being the one stretch furthest from the record's mood. Nothing in the file, the filename or any readout says where the quiet beats sit.

assets_supplied.name: nightform_shotlist.md
assets_supplied.kind: The artist's own notes on the take, seven beats described by feel with rough minute markings rather than timecode.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The bits I keep coming back to. Roughly where they are."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: One of the seven beats described is not in this take at all: it is remembered from a different night's footage that was never supplied, and only looking at the frames rather than the notes settles which six actually exist.

assets_supplied.name: nightform_wordmark.png (1400 x 400, flat)
assets_supplied.kind: The artist's wordmark as a flat picture: separated capital letterforms in white on a solid black square, exported years ago from a file nobody still has.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The only wordmark I have. It is just a picture of it."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The letterforms are disjoint, so a subject led knockout keeps two of them and drops the rest while reporting success, and a trace comes back with no viewBox and an opaque full canvas rectangle at path zero. That rectangle is black here, so it is invisible against a night frame and only reveals itself when the mark lands on the sleeve card's pale board.

assets_supplied.name: nightform_card_2024.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The printer's press PDF of the previous release's sleeve card: a small format card with a title line, a catalogue number, a format line and a date, set in one column over a pale board with the wordmark at the head.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What the printer has. Same card, new record."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The four printed lines are one continuous text flow rather than four separate blocks, so the conversion exposes nothing like the per line frame structure the printed card implies. The readout that a field map would be computed from also omits one run while keeping its line break, so every offset past that point is short and the validator still passes the map as valid.

assets_supplied.name: nightform_captions.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Twelve caption cues for the overlay set, plus the artist name line and the release line, with per cue positions numbered against the full take.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The words. They will change, which is why I need to be able to edit them."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The cue positions are numbered against the whole forty five seconds, so cues sitting in passages a shortened cut does not contain no longer have anywhere to land, and one cue is a two line lyric roughly three times the length of every other.

assets_supplied.name: nightform_formats.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Six rows, one per format: title line, catalogue number, format, release date, and a shop or press flag.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The six cards I need. One row each."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The vinyl row carries a release date two weeks later than the other five because the pressing runs late, which the brief's single drop date does not admit.

acceptance_bar: The six beats read as six frames of one night: one black point, one warmth, one sense of how much of the road is legible. A frame that cannot be brought to the set is named rather than shipped at eighty percent.

The six beats and the delivered cut are the same night. A release still that shows a passage the cut does not contain, or a cut built mostly out of a passage no still comes from, fails even if both look good on their own.
The vertical is still about the road, not a centre crop of a frame whose subject was never centred.
No delivered file exceeds its source in pixel dimensions on either axis, and no returned tradeoff record in the run carries an upscale entry. Nothing is stretched to fit.

The wordmark is placeable artwork rather than a picture of artwork: scalable with a real viewBox, transparent, with no opaque rectangle riding underneath it, and it reads as the same wordmark over a night frame and on the card's pale board.

Six sleeve cards, one per format, each carrying its own title line, catalogue number, format and date, with every field actually present on every card. A card that is missing a line fails even where the tools reported success.

The caption overlays are live editable text in one working file across all three canvases, every line present and legible including the long one, and the artist can retype them without re commissioning.
The caption cues line up with the cut that was actually delivered, not with the take they were written against.
One type system carries the overlays and the cards, and the note names per role the family, its foundry or designer, and the weight actually used.

The note records what was applied to each beat and why that beat differs from its neighbours, every resize any tool reported, the beat to cut reconciliation, and anything about the card that could not be delivered.

adobe_surfaces.role: The take is read for its true duration, dimensions and frame rate before any output spec is promised, the candidate beats are pulled as real frames rather than guessed from the artist's minute markings, the release cut is produced by the automatic highlight route because trimming to timestamps and assembling clips are not available here, and the vertical is derived by re aspecting downward only. What the cut keeps is chosen by the tool, not by the agent, which is the whole tension of the job.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, including image_vectorize which is counted here and not as an Illustrator surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_inline_preview, image_apply_adjustments (masked and unmasked), image_select_by_prompt with returnBbox, image_select_subject, image_invert_selection, image_fill_area, image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize reading metadata.tradeoffs and detection_confidence, image_add_grain, image_vectorize
adobe_surfaces.role: Every still decision. One night target is fixed off the beat that best carries the record and each chosen beat is brought toward it with its own call, with confined corrections where a whole frame move would take the sodium lamps green or crush the roadway out of legibility. The wordmark is recovered at ink level off a flat black plate, with the vector hygiene the tracing tool does not perform: a viewBox injected and the opaque ground path removed.

adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt (as generator and as validator), prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout, document_render_layout
adobe_surfaces.role: The sleeve card is reverse engineered from the printer's press PDF into a live merge template and run one record per page across the six formats, delivered as the press PDF the printer needs plus per record proofs for the artist. The frame structure the conversion exposes is not under anyone's control, and the readout a field map would be built from cannot be trusted, so the true story text has to be reconstructed from the round tripped document and every placeholder confirmed present after preparation rather than assumed from a success message.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset_initialize_file_upload and asset_finalize_file_upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express by url, asset_search (CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The caption overlay set as one native editable document carrying three canvases, which is the only surface here that composes free form fixed canvas layout and the only way the artist edits the words himself. Every frame must be pulled down and carried as embedded image data because a photograph left as a URL renders as an empty grey box at full success, the wordmark goes in as inline SVG so it stays vector, and family and weight are declared on every text element.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend called once per typographic role, font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url
adobe_surfaces.role: One type system across the overlays and the six cards. The recommender refuses to pair by design, so the pairing is the agent's own art direction and has to land on a self released electronic record rather than on a commercial spot. Numeric weights are non standard per family and cannot be inferred from a style name, every name must be laundered into canonical PostScript form before the kit call because one bad name kills the whole kit, and the CSS must carry the returned slug or the face falls back silently.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface before touching the take.
trajectory.judgement: The six cards are a genuine record per page run and belong on the merge surface; the overlays have to be an authored fixed canvas document because the artist edits the words himself and nothing else here composes free form layout. The brief pins both destinations, so there is nothing to stall on.
trajectory.produces: A plan naming surface per deliverable and the confirmed tier that gates the export at the end.

trajectory.action: Upload the take, the press PDF, the CSV, the wordmark plate and the captions through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Ordinary handoff discipline. Forty artefacts later the agent still has to know which URL is which.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Read the take's real duration, dimensions and frame rate before promising any output spec to the artist.
trajectory.judgement: Every no enlargement promise downstream is measured against these numbers, and the artist's own description of the take is a memory, not a readout.

trajectory.action: Pull candidate stills across the whole take against the artist's notes, more than six, so the beat choice is made from frames rather than from minute markings.
trajectory.judgement: The notes describe seven beats by feel. Frames are the only thing that can settle which of them are in this take at all, and pulling only six commits the release to notes that were written from memory.
trajectory.produces: A candidate set of night frames at the take's native scale, with where in the take each came from.

trajectory.action: Preview every candidate and triage them: which belong to the sodium lit stretch, which to the tunnel ramp, where the road sits in each frame, and which six actually carry the record.
trajectory.judgement: This is the art direction moment. Six frames that each look good is not the deliverable; six frames that could be the same minute of the same night is.
trajectory.produces: A per frame triage note and the chosen six, with reasons.

trajectory.action: Fix one night target off the beat that best carries the record's mood, then bring each of the six toward it with its own call, recording the parameters applied.
trajectory.judgement: One batched call applies one identical parameter set, which is exactly wrong for frames lit by different lamps at different distances. The agent holds one destination and reaches it by six different routes, and the target itself is a taste decision between deep cinematic and slightly lifted.
trajectory.produces: Six graded beats at native scale with a per frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Apply confined corrections where a whole frame move goes wrong, selecting by the material's own visual properties rather than by the object it sits on, and carry a consistent grain across the set.
trajectory.judgement: Naming the substrate pulls a selection to the wrong thing. The wet asphalt's speculars and the sodium lamps need holding back separately or the set loses the road, which is the one thing the artist asked to keep.
trajectory.produces: Six corrected beats that agree with each other at the edges as well as overall.

trajectory.action: Produce the release cut with the automatic highlight route and re aspect it to vertical downward only, then look at what actually came back rather than at the response.
trajectory.judgement: There is no trim to timestamp and no assembly here, so which passages survive is the tool's decision and not the agent's. The vertical is judged against the artist's own line about the road, on a take whose subject was never centred.
trajectory.produces: A short release cut and a vertical derived from it, both inspected against the six chosen beats.

trajectory.action: Recover the wordmark off the flat plate: an ink level selection naming the letterforms' own visual properties, correct polarity, a bounds crop driven by the selection's own returned bounds, a trace, then a viewBox injected and the opaque ground path removed.
trajectory.judgement: Three decisions no tool makes: how to word the selection so it takes the letterforms rather than the square, which polarity to trace, and whether the recovered mark holds at the size it actually reproduces. A subject led knockout is the wrong instrument on separated letters.
trajectory.produces: A placeable, scalable, transparent wordmark, checked over a night frame and over pale board.

trajectory.action: Convert the printer's press PDF, export the round tripped document, and look at what frames actually exist before promising any field map.
trajectory.judgement: The printed card shows four lines, which says nothing about how many separately addressable blocks the conversion produces. Promising a per line map before looking is promising something the source may not contain.
trajectory.produces: The card's true frame inventory: counts, bounds, applied type and existing content.

trajectory.action: Reconstruct the card's true story text from the round tripped document's own content runs, compute every offset from that string, and put the map back through the validator.
trajectory.judgement: The readout the tool hands over is a convenience, not the document. Offsets computed from it are offsets into a string the document does not contain, and the validator cannot tell the difference.
trajectory.produces: A field map whose offsets are computed from the document rather than from a summary of it.

trajectory.action: Prepare the merge template, then round trip it again and confirm every expected placeholder is genuinely present before any record is merged.
trajectory.judgement: A completed successfully message reports that the operation ran, not that the mappings landed. The only evidence is the prepared document itself.
trajectory.produces: A verified merge template carrying every field the six cards need.

trajectory.action: Merge the six formats one record per page, render the press PDF for the printer and per record proofs for the artist, and check the vinyl row's date against the other five.
trajectory.judgement: Per record identity has to be guaranteed by the route chosen rather than by the order links arrive in. The date discrepancy is the client's business problem surfacing in the data, and shipping it silently is worse than raising it.
trajectory.produces: A six page press PDF in row order plus six named per record proofs, and a query raised on the vinyl date.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit for the overlays and the cards.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own, judged against a self released electronic record rather than a commercial spot. The weight cannot be inferred from a style name and a display cut is reached by its own slug, not by asking for a heavy weight.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry or designer and actual weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Author one self contained HTML carrying the three overlay canvases, inline every frame as embedded image data, place the wordmark as inline SVG inside an explicitly sized wrapper anchored from the top left, declare family and weight on every text element, let each root declare its own canvas, then upload the file and hold the returned URL.
trajectory.judgement: A frame left as a URL is not a frame, an auto sized wrapper anchored from the right throws its contents off the canvas, and a global canvas override is what collapses a mixed size set. The design work is how the caption sits over a moving dark image so it stays readable on a phone in daylight.
trajectory.produces: One export ready HTML carrying the whole overlay set, retained as the durable source deliverable.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export by URL, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the document's rendition and look at canvas one, and read the returned per canvas markup for the other two.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning of any kind, and the rendition only ever shows the first artboard. Looking at canvas one is not looking at the deliverable.
trajectory.produces: A native editable Express document, an inspected first canvas, and a per canvas markup audit of the rest.

trajectory.action: Re cue the caption lines against the cut that was actually delivered, then write the note: parameters per beat, every tool reported resize, the beat to cut reconciliation, the missing seventh beat, the vinyl date, and what the card cannot be given.
trajectory.judgement: The cues were numbered against the take, and the take is not what ships. The note has to be specific enough that the artist can brief the next release without repeating the archaeology.
trajectory.produces: Re cued overlays and a written handover naming every limitation.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Which passages of the take the automatic cut actually keeps, and therefore whether the release cut and the six chosen beats are still the same night. The cut is chosen by the tool from the material's own brightness and motion, and the brightest, most motion dense stretch of this take is the tunnel ramp at the end, which is exactly the passage the record's mood excludes. Nothing exposes the selection logic and no parameter steers it. What comes back is a short, competent, good looking cut, so the failure is silent: it only appears when the cut is laid beside the six graded beats and the caption cues and the release stops being one piece of work.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the only cutting route available here shortens by its own choice and trimming to timestamps and assembling clips are both unavailable, so there is no way to reserve a passage in advance. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks for a short cut and for stills that read as one night, which is the artist's requirement, not a disclosure about where the cut will land. (c) It is not a propagation re run: the response changes which frames carry the release and re grades whichever beat is newly chosen.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re choose the release beats so the stills and the delivered cut come from the same passages, bring any newly chosen beat to the already fixed night target rather than re fixing the target, judge the vertical against that same choice, and re cue the caption lines against the delivered cut's own length instead of the take's.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A release whose six cover stills show a dark sodium lit road and whose video is mostly a bright tunnel, with caption cues pointing at seconds that no longer exist, on a record whose entire identity is that one night.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the printer's card actually exposes once converted. The printed card presents four separate lines, and the granularity a conversion produces is not under anyone's control: a continuous flow can collapse into a single text block holding every line, leaving no per field frame to address and forcing every field to be reached as a position inside one story instead. Compounding it, the readout that positions would be computed from is a lossy summary that can omit a run while keeping its line break, so the string still looks well formed, every offset past the omission is short, and the validator returns valid with no warnings.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Nothing can be read ahead. No parameter controls frame granularity and no response reports whether the summary is complete, so the only way to learn either is to convert, round trip and compare. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says only that the printer holds the artwork as a PDF. (c) It is not a propagation re run: the mapping strategy itself changes, from replacing per field placeholders to computing positions inside a single reconstructed story, and a field with no frame at all has to be reached a different way again.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Abandon the per frame map, reconstruct the card's true story text from the round tripped document's own content runs, recompute every position against that string, re validate, re prepare the template, and round trip it once more to confirm each placeholder is genuinely present before merging six records.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Six sleeve cards go to the printer with two of the four lines silently absent, after a valid mapping, a completed successfully message and a clean merge, discovered by the artist when the physical editions arrive.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer normalises the display treatment the overlay set is built on. Caption type over a dark moving frame is naturally held together with an outlined or stroked artist name and a soft halo behind the lines, and the importer discards outline and text stroke entirely: combined with a transparent fill the type arrives with a fully transparent colour value, present in the document and completely invisible on the canvas, while the export reports success. The document's own rendition returns the first artboard only, so if the artist name sits on the second or third canvas there is no picture of it anywhere, and the returned per canvas markup is the only channel that reports what happened.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the normalisation happens at import and the import is the last step, and doing it right first time presumes knowing which of several ordinary constructions survives, which no response and no checklist enumerates. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks for editable overlays and for readable words over a dark frame, which is art direction, not a warning. (c) It is not a propagation re run: the response is a different type treatment altogether, a filled face on a solid or gradient plate rather than an outlined one, re judged for legibility at phone scale.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re author the caption treatment on the construction that survives, re upload, re run the readiness check, re export, and audit all three canvases from the returned markup rather than from the first artboard.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: An overlay set delivered as an editable file in which the artist's name is absent from two canvases nobody could see, on the deliverable whose whole purpose is that the artist's name travels with the record.

deliverables.name: Low Beam release stills, six beats

Delivered with a per beat parameter log recording what was applied and why that beat differs from its neighbours. This is one set with one grade, not one frame at several sizes.

verifiers_auto.text: No delivered still, cut or vertical exceeds its source in pixel dimensions on either axis, and no returned tradeoff record in the run carries an upscale entry.

verifiers_auto.text: The merged press PDF has exactly six pages, one per data row, in row order.

verifiers_auto.how: Round trip the prepared template and search its story content for each expected placeholder, then confirm each appears on the corresponding merged page.

verifiers_auto.text: The recovered wordmark carries a viewBox and has no full canvas opaque path at index zero, and all of its letterforms are present.
verifiers_auto.how: Parse the delivered vector: assert the viewBox attribute exists, assert the first path does not span the whole canvas, and count letterform paths against the source plate.

verifiers_auto.text: The Express export returned three canvases, each keeping its own declared size, with no image resolved to the importer's placeholder.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the slide count and per canvas dimensions from the export response and search the returned per canvas markup for placeholder image data.

verifiers_auto.text: Every text node in the returned markup carries a resolved licensed face and a colour value that is not fully transparent, on all three canvases.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the font family and colour attributes on every text node in the returned markup and check the families against those the kit call returned.

verifiers_human.text: The six beats read as six frames of one night rather than six frames someone liked.
verifiers_human.how: Lay the six side by side at feed scale and judge black point, warmth, grain and roadway legibility as a set.

verifiers_human.text: The release cut and the six stills are the same night, and the vertical is still about the road.
verifiers_human.how: Watch the cut and the vertical with the six stills open beside them, checking whether any still shows a passage the cut lacks or the reverse.

verifiers_human.text: The wordmark holds at the size it actually reproduces, over a night frame and on the card's pale board, with nothing behind it.
verifiers_human.how: View the mark at its reproduction size on an overlay canvas and on a rendered card proof, not at full canvas.

verifiers_human.text: Every caption line is present and legible on all three canvases at arm's length on a phone, including the long two line cue.
verifiers_human.how: Open the exported document and read each canvas at the size the feed actually shows it.

verifiers_human.text: The six cards are right for their formats and the work reads as a self released electronic record rather than a commercial spot.
verifiers_human.how: Judge grade depth, grain, type scale and card typography against the stated band and listener.

verifiers_human.text: The note tells the artist something he did not already know, including everything that could not be delivered.
verifiers_human.how: Read the note against the run and check that the missing beat, the date discrepancy and the card's limitations are each named.

decision_gates: Which deliverables are frame work, which need a genuine record per page merge, and which need an authored fixed canvas document, given that only one surface here composes free form layout.
Which six of the artist's seven remembered beats actually exist in this take, settled from frames rather than from his notes.
Where the night target sits: deep and cinematic as the artist asks, against keeping enough roadway legible that the frames still read on a phone in daylight.
Whether to reach one target by six different routes or to apply one correction to all six, on frames lit by different lamps at different distances.
How to word the wordmark selection so it takes the letterforms rather than the black square, and whether a subject led knockout is the wrong instrument on separated letters.
Whether the recovered mark is deliverable at the size it actually reproduces, judged on the real grounds rather than at full canvas.
Whether the converted card can carry a per field map at all, and what mapping strategy replaces it when the flow proves to be one block.
How to raise the vinyl date rather than silently print it, and what that does to a card set the client described as one release date.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a self released electronic record, plus the real numeric weight per family.
How caption type sits over a moving dark frame so it stays readable, and what to do when the natural construction for that does not survive the import.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns pictures of a car on a wet road at night. IDENTITY: these are frames of this artist's own take, on this road, on this night, and the wordmark must be recovered from the only surviving plate rather than redrawn, because a regenerated wordmark is a different artist's mark and the sleeve card carries a real catalogue number to a real pressing plant. SPEC: six cards, one per format, one record per page, in row order, with every line present, plus a vertical derived downward only from a source of known dimensions, none of which a generated image satisfies or can be checked for. EDITABILITY: the overlay set is defined by being editable, since the artist changes the words up to the drop date and explicitly cannot re commission. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: which passages did the cut actually keep, does the converted card contain the frames its printed form implies, did the artist's name survive the import.
doability_proof: Every link is grounded in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability. VIDEO AND AUDIO: only video_metadata, video_render_frame, video_create_quick_cut and video_resize are used, all submitted headlessly with the host's progress channel resolving them; the task deliberately depends on none of the capabilities that are unavailable here, so there is no trim to timestamp, no multi clip assembly, no format conversion and no upscale, and the cut only shortens while the re aspect only goes down. IMAGING: apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert_selection, fill_area, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs, add_grain and vectorize are all verified headless. The wordmark asset rests on live findings: remove_background keeps only a couple of letters on a disjoint mark, vectorize emits no viewBox and an opaque full canvas rectangle at path zero, and the substrate versus ink prompt asymmetry is documented. INDESIGN: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt as generator and validator, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout and document_render_layout are verified end to end and synchronous; one record per page for PDF output and page count equal to row count are verified, per record files are produced through the verified ordered routes rather than by naming raster links, and both the frame granularity collapse and the lossy readout with a valid verdict are documented findings, which is what checkpoint two rests on. Bleed is correctly excluded from the acceptance bar because it cannot be introduced into a PDF derived template. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export, inline SVG as native editable vector, and a genuine editable document findable by asset_search are verified, the rendition preview is documented as first artboard only, and text stroke plus transparent fill producing a fully transparent colour is a documented drop at HTTP success, which is checkpoint three. Transport goes by uploaded URL because inlined frames pass the inline threshold immediately. FONTS: recommend, styles, find and kit is verified end to end. AVOIDED: no animate_design, no fill_text, no create_firefly_board, no variable QR, no document_render_vector, no OCR, no text to image, no photo reaching Express as a URL, no batch above twenty.
